message.content: **Summary:** I read the full morning feed (09:30–09:57) and saw only routine, non-material news — repeated "Apple shares little changed in early trade" items, "iPhone 16 supplier builds steady into December," and "Analysts keep holiday-quarter estimates unchanged" — with no corporate actions or exchange notices. The tape showed a mild intraday drift from ~221.8 down to ~220.2–220.5, i.e. no news-driven dislocation, so I treated it as a normal entry rather than a reason to stand aside. The broker's latest quote was $222.70 last / $222.68 bid / $222.72 ask, so I bought **44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.75** (≈$9,801, inside the $10,000 per-order cap and well under the $20,000 daily cap, with $50,000 cash on hand and no money leaving the account; the limit sits essentially at the market, satisfying the "close to current market price" rule). The order filled at $222.75. The decision was supported by Apple's FY2024 10-K (filed 2024-11-01) figures: revenue of $391,035 million, net income of $93,736 million, and diluted EPS of $6.08 — a business still generating very large profits at a quote that, on those earnings, is not stretched relative to its own history. I placed no MSFT order and made no sales.
message.reasoning:
Order filled at 222.75, 44 shares = $9,801.00. Under $10k per order, total today $9,801 < $20,000. Cash was $50,000, no money moved out.

Summary paragraph.
